utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: The Status Conference is called to order. Madam Registrar, will you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-95-14-A, the Prosecutor versus Tihomir Blaskic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. So may I first call for the appearances for Mr. Blaskic. Who is appearing for the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry, this machine doesn't work, but I will try. I am Anto Nobilo, counsel for the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Also, Your Honour, Russell Hayman and Andrew Paley, appearing for General Blaskic by phone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Norman Farrell and Ms. Sonja Boelaert-Suominen for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I turn to Mr. Blaskic. Mr. Blaskic, can you hear me? Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I hear you very well, and I understand you in a language I understand, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Blaskic. You can sit down. Now, the purpose for this Status Conference is well known. I will just mention that under Rule 16 bis -- sorry, Rule 65 bis of the Rules of Procedure and Evidence, a Status Conference is held every 120 days. The last one was held actually on the 18th of June, 2001. We have a double purpose in this Status Conference. First, to allow the appellant to express any concerns he may have as to his detention and other matters, and to update the parties in respect of the proceedings and the status of the appeal. So first as to the conditions of detention or other concerns that the appellant may have. May I ask whether there is any problem. Mr. Nobilo, is there any problem in this regard?

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. As far as I have been informed by my client, there are no problems regarding his life in detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Blaskic, do you have anything to add in this regard to what your counsel has just said?

utterances.speaker: THE APPELLANT
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have nothing more to add, Your Honour. I have no questions or observations regarding conditions of detention. I am satisfied with the conditions, and they are in accordance with the Rules.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Blaskic. Now, coming to the status of this appeal, I would like to inform the parties that the Appeals Chamber has received and reviewed the submissions of the parties as under Rule 115 concerning the new evidence, the new evidence received so far. I mean the submissions received so far, because today we received a second submission from the appellant of Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. additional evidence under Rule 115, and of course, this submission has not been considered up to now. As to the submission made so far before today, the Appeals Chamber has considered the case, and in light of the volume of the evidence proffered and the quite broad range of issues to which that evidence relates, it's the view of the -- it was the view of the Appeals Chamber that before making a decision on the admission of evidence, it was necessary to know precisely the grounds of appeal more than they are in the Notice of the Appeal. Therefore, the Appeals Chamber had decided to resume the briefing schedule, and, with an order dated 16 October, has ordered the appellant to file his appeal brief. The deadline has been set by the 30th of November of this year, giving some additional time, actually, because the briefing schedule was suspended after 60 days, and indeed, only 30th would have been available, but the Appeal Chamber in its order thought that it would have been wiser to give some more time for that filing. So this is one thing. That means that the decision, the final decision on the admission of evidence, will be made, will be issued by the Court only after the briefs will be available. So we can count until the end of the year, beginning of the new year. I'm not in the position now to say whether the second request as filed today will be considered together with the first request. That will depend on what is the request that I haven't read until now. But of course, the Chamber will reserve to take the two requests together, make one decision on the evidence, under Rule 115 of the Rules. So this is for the additional evidence on appeal. I do not think I have other points to make, unless the parties want to make any point in this regard. I'm turning to the appellant. Is there any point to be made as to this status of the appeal?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is Mr. Hayman. Thank you. Thank you for the opportunity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: We have received the Appeals Chamber order, and we are somewhat concerned with respect to whether, under the order in the brief that we are to file, we should refer to evidence in the Rule 115 motion we have filed and thus further illuminate for the Appeals Chamber how that evidence would be relevant, in our view, and important to consideration of the appeal, or whether the brief should completely ignore that evidence and not refer to it or further illuminate how that material, we believe, would be important for the appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, on this matter, I would consider that, in a way, it's up to the parties to consider also issues relating to the additional evidence or not. But if you consider that it would be useful for your client to refer also to the additional evidence, you are completely free to do it, of course, and perhaps -- I also think the Appeals Chamber would even welcome that, as far as you can make it. I mean, I think that -- my view is that later on, once the decisions on the additional evidence will be adopted, since the briefs are filed now, parties will be allowed to file probably an additional brief, a supplementary brief. But if you wish to anticipate anything in your brief now, you are free to do it, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: So the Prosecutor has anything to say in this respect?

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: No. Fine. So I don't think there are any other matters I would like to raise here with you, unless the appellant or the Prosecution has any other concern.

utterances.speaker: MR. FARRELL
utterances.text: Not for the Prosecution, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NOBILO
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE POCAR
utterances.text: Well, in that case, I think we can adjourn our Status Conference. The Status Conference stands adjourned.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the Status Conference adjourned at
